stack.name: Physical
stack.note: instances plus 15 schema nodes for the class hierarchy

stack.name: Abstract views
stack.note: VW_ONT_* span several concrete types in one query

stack.name: Semantic
stack.note: base for concrete lookups, ontology for cross-type, metadata for governance

stack.name: Agent
stack.note: routes a question to the right layer

classes.name: Asset
classes.description: A physical production asset with a health state.

classes.name: BusinessProcess
classes.description: An SAP end-to-end process, e.g. Design to Operate.

classes.name: CDSEntity
classes.description: A CDS view exposed by a data product.

classes.name: CatalogObject
classes.description: An SAP Business Data Cloud catalog artefact. Kept as a separate branch: it describes what data exists, not what the supply chain is.

classes.name: ComponentLot
classes.description: A received supplier lot of a BOM component, with inspection result.

classes.name: Customer
classes.description: An organisation that receives finished output.

classes.name: DataProduct
classes.description: A BDC data product exposing CDS entities.

classes.name: Entity
classes.description: Anything the supply-chain ontology can talk about.

classes.name: Equipment
classes.description: A production tool (stepper, etcher, CVD chamber, assembly cell) at a work center.

classes.name: Facility
classes.description: A physical site with capacity. Abstract: the network has only plants today, but distribution centres and contract manufacturers are the same kind of thing.

classes.name: InboundFlow
classes.description: Supplier to plant.

classes.name: InterPlantFlow
classes.description: Plant to plant. The mechanism by which a disruption travels.

classes.name: Item
classes.description: A traceable physical unit.

classes.name: MaterialCategory
classes.description: A class of material the network moves. Sole-source risk is a property of a category, not of a plant, which is why it needs to be its own class.

classes.name: MaterialFlow
classes.description: A recurring movement of one material category between two entities, carrying monthly volume and value. Reified as a class because the flow itself has attributes the endpoints do not.

classes.name: OutboundFlow
classes.description: Plant to customer. Where revenue is at risk.

classes.name: Party
classes.description: An external organisation the network trades with. Abstract, so a question about 'who is affected' can span suppliers and customers in one answer.

classes.name: Plant
classes.description: A manufacturing site. Carries capacity (work centres, hours, spare units) and inventory (days of cover, stock value) as properties, because both are 1:1 with the plant rather than entities in their own right.

classes.name: SalesOrder
classes.description: A customer order line for an inspection system, with OTIF outcome and late cost.

classes.name: Supplier
classes.description: An organisation that ships material into a plant.

classes.name: SystemSerial
classes.description: One built inspection system, identified by serial number.

classes.name: Transaction
classes.description: A business document that commits the supply chain to deliver.

relations.name: associatedWith
relations.description: A declared association between two CDS entities.

relations.name: canSubstituteFor
relations.description: Two plants can substitute for each other on a category both produce. INFERRED by rule from `produces` — not stored anywhere. 8 pairs today: Inspection Systems across 3 plants, Metrology across 2.

relations.name: carriesCategory
relations.description: A material flow carries one material category.

relations.name: containsLot
relations.description: Component lots consumed in the system (genealogy).

relations.name: containsProduct
relations.description: A business process contains data products.

relations.name: exposesEntity
relations.description: A data product exposes CDS entities.

relations.name: flowsTo
relations.description: Material moves from one entity to another. Abstract parent of the three concrete flow types, so a traversal can follow any of them.

relations.name: fulfilledBy
relations.description: The plant that builds and ships the order.

relations.name: installedAt
relations.description: The plant where a tool is installed.

relations.name: placedBy
relations.description: The customer who placed the order.

relations.name: produces
relations.description: A plant is qualified to produce a material category. 11 plant-category pairs across 8 categories.

relations.name: sharesCanonicalObject
relations.description: Two data products reference the same canonical ODM object.

relations.name: shippedOn
relations.description: The order the system shipped against.

relations.name: shipsTo
relations.description: A plant ships finished output to a customer.

relations.name: supplies
relations.description: A supplier ships material into a plant.

relations.name: transfersTo
relations.description: A plant transfers material to another plant. The path a disruption follows.
